key_insight: Machine learning can accurately predict band gap energies across multiple halide perovskite families using simple atomic and structural descriptors, revealing which composition factors matter most.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a fast screening tool for designing low-toxicity perovskites with targeted optoelectronic band gaps, reducing reliance on trial-and-error synthesis.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based models on atomic and structural features.
Compared RFR, GBRT, and XGB for band gap prediction.
Used feature importance to identify dominant B-site and X-site descriptors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy across several model types and highlights consistent feature-importance trends across diverse halide perovskite compositions.
watch_item: Model performance may depend on the representativeness of the training dataset, so extrapolation to unexplored compositions should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
